title: Mara and the Monsoon
premise: Zephyrine Winterbourne, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Meridian Syndicate, is hired by his old rival Odile Vasseur to escort her upriver to the source of the Kalyani River—a place his old crew swore off after a monsoon killed two of their own twelve years ago. As the crew battles flooded gorges, hostile settlements, and their own buried grief, Zephyrine discovers Odile's true goal: proof that the Syndicate engineered the dam collapse that destroyed his hometown, evidence that could break them. In the climax, as the monsoon makes landfall at the forbidden source, Zephyrine must choose between destroying the evidence to save his crew or broadcasting it and finally paying the full price of survival; he chooses justice, loses the money, and gains something rarer—a crew that chooses him back.
about_author: Marguerite Delacroix is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent a decade mapping waterways across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people outrunning their pasts, usually in bad weather.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector's Umbrella
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. In a rain-soaked port city, a polite Syndicate enforcer reminds Zephyrine of what he owes, giving him thirty days. He measures his life in miles driven, not years lived. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: An Offer from Odile
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Old rival Odile Vasseur appears with a contract: guide her crew upriver to the Kalyani's forbidden source before monsoon landfall. The route passes through territory his dead crewmates swore off. Emotional beat: temptation wrapped in old wounds.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: POV Tomas, the navigator. Zephyrine assembles a skeleton crew—Tomas, engineer Priya, and teenage deckhand Wren—who each owe him or need him. They sign on despite the rumors about the upper Kalyani. Emotional beat: fragile loyalty forming.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Miles
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine, flashback-heavy. We learn how the monsoon flood of twelve years ago killed Mara and Dev, how the crew scattered, and why Zephyrine stopped staying anywhere. Emotional beat: grief revealed as the engine of his restlessness.

chapters.title: Departure at Low Water
chapters.summary: POV Priya. The boat launches ahead of schedule because Syndicate shadows are following them. First rapids test the crew; Odile proves competent but secretive about her cargo. Emotional beat: uneasy momentum.

chapters.title: The Drowned Town
chapters.summary: POV Wren. They pass a settlement half-swallowed by a reservoir and stop for fuel. Wren, seeing displaced families, begins asking questions no one wants answered. Emotional beat: innocence confronting cost.

chapters.title: What Odile Carries
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Zephyrine catches Odile photographing documents; she reveals partially that she's investigating the dam upstream—and that the Syndicate built it. He refuses to believe it connects to his town. Emotional beat: denial cracking.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at Serpent Bend
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. A Syndicate toll post blocks the gorge; the crew talks their way through using forged papers, but the enforcer from chapter one logs their passage. Emotional beat: the net tightening.

chapters.title: River People
chapters.summary: POV Priya. The crew shelters with an isolated river community living outside all law, governed by their own flood-season justice. Priya, an exile herself, finds belonging here—and warns Zephyrine that some prices can't be paid twice. Emotional beat: warmth with foreboding.

chapters.title: Mara's Reach
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. They enter the exact stretch of river where Mara died. Zephyrine freezes at the helm; only Wren's steady hands get them through. That night he tells Wren about Mara. Emotional beat: confession as survival.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Someone loosens the fuel lines overnight. Suspicion splits the crew—Odile accuses Tomas, Tomas accuses Odile. Zephyrine realizes the Syndicate has an informant aboard. Emotional beat: trust fracturing.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Bells
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. A brutal portage through a gorge hung with warning bells left by the river people. An ambush by Syndicate hired guns costs them supplies and nearly Wren. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Half-Truths at the Fire
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Odile admits she was Syndicate once—that she helped build the ledger proving the dam collapse was deliberate, engineered to seize the valley. She needs the source gauges to prove it. Emotional beat: guilt offered as alliance.

chapters.title: The Informant
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Zephyrine deduces the informant is Priya, coerced via her family's debts. Instead of casting her out, he uses her channel to feed false positions. Emotional beat: mercy as strategy.

chapters.title: Landfall Warning
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Satellite reports confirm the monsoon will make landfall in four days—two days sooner than planned. The Syndicate convoy is behind them but closing. Emotional beat: the clock becoming a character.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. They reach the source basin: a high valley where the river begins, ringed by the great dam and its sealed station. The beauty of it undoes Zephyrine—he grew up downstream of this water. Emotional beat: awe braided with rage.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Inside the station, Odile retrieves the original engineering ledgers proving the collapse was ordered. Alarms trigger; the Syndicate team arrives led by the enforcer. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into trap.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: POV Wren. To cover their escape, the Syndicate opens spillway gates early—the monsoon arriving as a weapon. The crew fights through flooding tunnels; Wren saves Priya, repaying every debt between them. Emotional beat: courage under rising water.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Crest
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Trapped on the dam crest, Zephyrine holds the only copy of the ledgers. The enforcer offers to erase his debt in exchange for burning them. Zephyrine instead broadcasts the ledger files on the station's emergency band and lets the pages go into the flood. Emotional beat: sacrifice as answer.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. The crew rides the flood downriver, battered but alive, while the broadcast spreads through every river town. The Syndicate's local power begins to crack; the enforcer retreats rather than be seen failing twice. Emotional beat: exhaustion edged with hope.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Weeks later, independent investigators arrive; the river people testify; warrants are issued. The debt dies with the Syndicate's legitimacy. Odile offers Zephyrine a partnership; he declines—but asks her to stay in touch. Emotional beat: quiet vindication.

chapters.title: Years, Not Miles
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Zephyrine stays one full season at the river settlement, fixing boats and teaching Wren the river. For the first time in twelve years, he measures time in seasons, not miles. When the next storm season comes, the crew sets out together—not fleeing, but choosing. Emotional beat: belonging earned.
